concept.name: Credit spread
concept.definition: The difference between the yield on the debt securities of a particular corporate or sovereign borrower (or a rating class of borrowers) and the yield on similar-maturity Treasury securities. It compensates investors for bearing default and credit-migration risk, plus a liquidity component.
concept.intuition: It is the extra interest a risky borrower must pay over the government to persuade investors to lend to it.
concept.mechanics: Measured as corporate (or other non-Treasury) yield minus the matched-maturity Treasury yield, or at index level as an option-adjusted spread over the Treasury spot curve, e.g. the ICE BofA US Corporate Index OAS published on FRED.
concept.formula: Credit spread = y(corporate bond) − y(matched-maturity Treasury), in basis points.
concept.failure_modes: Spreads conflate expected default losses, risk premia, and illiquidity, so they overstate pure default compensation; in crises, liquidity-driven widening can look like surging default risk. Maturity or option mismatches also distort simple yield differences.
concept.misconceptions: The credit spread is not a direct estimate of default probability, and a high spread does not by itself imply a mispricing or an attractive trade.
concept.example: If BBB-rated 10-year corporate bonds yield 5.5% while the 10-year Treasury yields 4.3%, the credit spread is 120 basis points.

citations.source: CFTC Glossary (A Guide to the Language of the Futures Industry)
